lines.en: I walk into the cafe first thing in the morning to suddenly remember that I am not the only person of importance in Rin’s life.
What a shitty way to start the day.
Seated with her at the table appears to be the same girl we ran into at the park during her post-rejection blues.
Seated with her at the table is a girl around the same age as her, likely the one who she couldn’t stop talking about during the Christmas party.
The real question is whether or not I should leave the two of them alone or try to insert myself into the conversation.
I think back to what seems like aeons ago when I ran into a similar situation, but with Chika at the table next to Rin instead of this new girl.
Back then, Rin was barely able to hold a conversation on account of how nervous she was.
So...if something like that is happening again today, surely she’d want me to step in.
Right?
Well-
Only one way to find out, I guess.
Time to, once again, involve myself in the daily lives of [high_school] girls and see where I’m able to fit in.
: Oh, Sensei! Good morning.
: If you need anything, Haruka’s manning the counter right now.
: Sensei?
: You’re Rin’s teacher?
: You look younger than she made you sound.
: ...How did she make me sound, exactly?
: I have no idea what Otoha’s talking about.
: I totally didn’t say anything about the gigantic age gap between us and about how you’re way too comfortable around [teenage]girls.
: Yeah, you walked right up to us. Show some restraint, dude.
: Yeah, Sensei. Show some restraint.
Why am I being ganged up on before I’ve even had the chance to do anything?
: Oh, Sensei! Good morning!
: Hey, it’s that guy from the park who hangs out with [teenager]s.
: I liked Rin’s greeting more.
: Good morning, you two.
: If you need anything, Haruka is manning the counter right now.
: If not, you’re free to chill with us, though.
: Or both. You’re not limited to just one of those two things.
: I’d probably prefer it if you’d buy something. Otherwise it seems like you just came here to hang out with Rin.
: Oh, he probably did. He does that a lot.
: Stop saying things that give her a bad first impression of me.
: Second impression, Sensei. The first impression was when you were hanging out with Futaba and me in the park.
: Besides, we’re pals. I love that you come here to hang out.
: I still think it’s weird. But it is what it is, I guess. You do you, man.
: ...That aside, isn’t it too early for you to just be hanging out at a table instead of working?
: Normally, yeah. But I’m taking my break a little early since this is the only time Otoha is able to show up today.
: Wait, you’re doing this for me? Dude, how much longer is your shift after this?
: Like another seven hours or something. But it’s cool. I don’t need a break.
: I can drink coffee whenever I want, so I’ll just run on that until I collapse or something.
: Well shit, man. Now I feel really bad.
: I told you, it’s fine. I really don’t mind.
: What kind of life do you lead where nine in the morning is the only time you have to stop at a cafe?
: I live pretty much as far away from this side of town as possible, so it’s kind of a journey every time I need to come down.
: Otoha takes vocal lessons in some sketchy girl’s basement not far from here.
: She’s not sketchy...she’s a professional musician.
: She just has a really sketchy basement. I saw pictures.
: Yeah, that much is definitely true.
: She’s been a big help, though. I can’t imagine where I’d be without her.
: Right, you’re a musician.
: Still playing in that park we found you at?
: You’re a musician?
: Yup! Just like Rin here.
: Otoha is a million times better than me and I could never hope to achieve even an ounce of her talent or beauty.
: Also, I didn’t just mention her beauty. Forget that happened.
: Really, though. She’s so pretty.
: Please excuse Rin. She talks a little too much when she gets nervous.
: Yeah, that’s one of the first things I realized about her. I just ignore it at this point.
: Otoha used to play mini concerts every weekend at some park in the area Futaba and I used to live in.
: That’s how I met her.
: Used to?
: Had to stop since I’ve been really busy lately.
: After my[school] sunk into the ground out of nowhere, I started being homeschooled instead.
: And, weirdly enough, it’s actually a little harder being homeschooled than it is going to actual[school].
: Yeah, I honestly can’t imagine anything easier than being in my class.
: Sensei hasn’t given us a single assignment in months. It’s awesome.
: I’m lucky if I can go a day without some ridiculous assignment.
: My parents are super strict about my education now that I’m not in[school] anymore.
: I’ve been trying to convince her to transfer into our[school] but she feels weird about moving into the dorms without having a roommate.
: Can’t she just stay in your room?
: I mean...I think there’s a rule about having no more than two girls in one room-
: Unless...we slept in the same bed and no one ever found out about it...
: You good?
: Huh?
: Where am I right now?
: So, you’re only in this part of town so you can go hang out and sing in some sketchy girl’s basement?
: Some girl’s sketchy basement. Slightly different, but you get the gist.
: Rin and I have been talking a lot ever since bumping into each other in the park, but I don’t really have a lot of time to ever hang out or anything like that.
: So the only chances we have to meet up involve me getting up mad early and sacrificing sleep in the name of friendship.
: She’s awesome, right?! Coming all the way over here just to see me!
: It’s not that big of a deal...
: But yeah, I guess I can be kind of awesome at times.
: I come here to see you all the time.
: Yeah, but I see you so much that I’m starting to become immune.
: Can you...become immune to people?
: Of course!
: You two really spend that much time together, huh?
: Yeah, but he’s only seen my boobs like once or twice so we’re probably not as close as you think we are.
: Why would you even say that?
: Say what? What did I say?
: I literally can’t remember. Am I having a stroke?
: I’m just going to pretend I didn’t hear that, so don’t even worry about it.
Good. I guess this Otoha girl is just as cool as she looks.
Which is pretty damn cool, not gonna lie.
Do you see how many rings she’s wearing?
: Hey, umm...you wouldn’t happen to have any free time tonight or something would you?
: It’s like...the weekend and stuff, so I can’t imagine your parents are making you study all day today.
: I might have some free time later on but like, I don’t really have the money to afford another bus trip.
: Maybe we could meet halfway? Like, walk around the mall for a little while or something?
: Uhhhhhhhhhh...or literally anywhere else. Malls are weird anyway. Like, who likes malls?
: What? I like malls. Plenty of people like malls.
: Yeah but like...there are so many...fluorescent lights and...shoe stores...
: Chika doesn’t normally work nights if that’s what you’re worried about.
: Dad! Are you trying to embarrass me?!
: ...Did you just call me Dad?
: I definitely heard her call you Dad.
: Yes! Because you’re doing a really “Dad” thing right now!
: So uhh...who's this Chika person anyway?
: Her.
: How did you pull up a picture of her that quickly?
: Also, where did your phone even come from?
: Don’t ask questions you don’t want to hear the answers to, Sensei.
: But...I do want to hear the answers.
: She’s hot.
: Painfully so.
: Why’s one person keeping you away from the mall, though? I don’t get it.
: Well...she’s not keeping me away...
: I’m...distancing myself for...personal reasons.
: Care to elaborate since you seem to actually understand Rin?
: I’m sure he’d be thrilled to tell you all about it considering he played such a big role in everything that went down.
: I...should probably stay out of this, to be honest.
: But...you’re literally the one who brought it up.
: Leave my dad out of this.
: As much as I’d love to explain things to you, it would probably be best if Rin told you herself.
: Yeah...it doesn’t look like that’s going to happen.
: Not yet. I need time to prepare.
: And to...delete pictures.
: But...um, since I don’t want to go to the mall, maybe I could just come over to...your place or something?
: I have some extra money for the bus and I kind of know my way around that part of town anyway, so...I could just stop by tonight?
: That’s sweet, but you don’t have to do that. It’s a crazy long trip to make that late at night.
: My house is kind of boring anyway, so I can’t imagine it would be any fun.
: How about you just text me tonight and we try to make plans sometime in the future?
: Does that work?
: Y-Yeah! Totally.
: I’ll text you all day and make like, all of the plans ever.
: Um...I mean, if you want to text me all day that’s fine. But I don’t think I’ll be able to respond right away a lot of the time.
: I will do my best to not think you hate me if you take too long to reply.
: Hey, if that’s what makes you happy...
: I’ve gotta get a move on, though. There’s a sketchy basement with my name on it and drinking caffeine before singing really isn’t a great idea anyway.
: Yeah, totally! That’s a thing I definitely knew!
: Um...have fun in the basement!
: Yeah. I will...do just that.
: Bye, Rin.
: And see you, Sensei.
: Thanks for only moderately creeping up the place this morning.
: That’s what I’m here for.
: Wild.
Otoha grabs her cup of coffee off the table and chugs the entire thing down despite how bad caffeine apparently is before singing.
Which is also a thing I definitely knew.
And Rin is now beaming with so much excitement and energy that she doesn’t even feel the need to bring up Chika.
: Why the ever-living fuck did you bring up Chika?
Oh. Nevermind, I guess.
: Your expression really does not match your tone right now.
: No, like really, though! Why did you do that?!
: You totally knew why I didn’t want to go to the mall and you brought it up anyway.
: And don’t say it’s because you’re my dad and you were trying to embarrass me!
: Yeah, that is definitely not a thing I was going to say. Stop calling me your dad.
: Fine! Then why were you being such a bad homie?
: I’m just now starting to get over Chika and every time I hear her name it adds like one more week to the time it will take for that to happen.
: And now I’ve just added another week. Thanks a lot, Sensei.
: I don’t know. I guess seeing you with Otoha made me feel like you were a little closer to being over her.
: Dude, Otoha doesn’t even know I’m bi yet.
: I am...pretty sure she does.
: But I do such an awesome job hiding it!
: What?! Why are you being so quiet all of a sudden?!
: You literally told her that you wanted her to sleep in your bed and that she was beautiful like five minutes ago.
: That actually happened?!
: I thought that was just in my head!
: It absolutely was not.
: I’m such a creep. Why do you even like me?
: Probably because I’m a creep, too.
: You really are. You’re a total weirdo.
: Remind me to never flash you again.
: Absolutely not. I embrace all future flashing.
: Dude, weird. You just told me you want me to flash you.
: Yes. I am not hiding that.
: Gross. Super gross. You’re the worst.
: Get out of here, Dad. And stop going through my underwear drawer while I’m at[school].
It isn’t long before Rin’s break comes to an end and I need to head back out into the street to find some other way to spend my time.
Even though she gave me shit about it, I think it’s safe to assume that Rin isn’t actually mad at me.
But a lot of that is probably due to the fact that it didn’t backfire.
Her friend seems really chill. The two of them would make a good couple.
So much so that I’m only mildly concerned about her becoming yet another barrier between Rin and me in the future.
Your daughter, Rin’s affection has increased to [rin_love]!
